primitives.name: Honesty Contract Repair Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Rule applied to every decision: a failure that asserts a product HONESTY contract is repaired in the CODE; a failure that asserts a design detail the owner deliberately replaced today is reconciled in the TEST with the changing commit named.
primitives.assumptions: Every failure in the system either violates a product honesty contract or alters a deliberate design element; repairs must be codified or tested.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When H > 0 and C = 0, system enters repair mode.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's Bayesian update mechanism where H represents observed contract violations and C/T represent corrective actions.
layer2.telemetry: Number of contract violations repaired in code vs. test suite.

primitives.assumptions: All operations begin with a verified baseline state; any deviation triggers rollback or re-sync.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When R < 1, system halts until G is restored.

layer2.mapping: Derived from GSE's state transition kernel, ensuring all actions are grounded in a consistent repository state.

primitives.name: Local-CI Disparity Resolver
primitives.verbatim_quote: The five extra local failures are environment artifacts and are filed as C-313 (they pass in CI).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L': 'Local test failure count (dimensionless)', 'CI': 'CI test failure count (dimensionless)', 'A': 'Environment artifact indicator (binary)'}
primitives.assumptions: Disparities between local and CI environments are due to non-reproducible artifacts, not functional issues.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When A = 1 and L ≠ CI, disparity is resolved via artifact tagging.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's anomaly detection model where A indicates environmental variance and L/CI are likelihood ratios.
layer2.telemetry: Count of environment-specific test failures and their classification.
